codeReview.summary: Solid implementation that fully covers all feature requirements: newsletter HTML integration with top/bottom positioning, rich text inline style conversion, XSS sanitization (sanitizeRichHTML + isSafeURL), TipTap editor external sync fix, and toolbar active state fix. 42 well-structured tests all passing. A few minor non-blocking observations.

issues.description: style attribute sanitization strips expression() but not url() with dangerous protocols. The comment on line 170 says 'strip any expression() or url() with dangerous protocols' but only expression() is actually stripped. A CSS url() containing javascript: could theoretically be injected via a style attribute. In practice this is low risk since email clients already strip CSS url() and the TipTap editor doesn't produce url() in styles.

<ol> is in ALLOWED_TAGS but not in ALLOWED_ATTRS, so any style attributes on <ol> elements will be silently dropped. convertTipTapToInlineHTML in promotion-email-html.ts doesn't handle <ol> either, so ordered lists in the editor won't have inline styles in email output. TipTap's StarterKit includes OrderedList extension by default.

isSafeURL returns true when URL parsing fails (catch block). This means malformed URLs like 'javascript:alert(1)' that bypass the URL constructor would pass through. In practice, 'javascript:alert(1)' is a valid URL that the constructor parses correctly, so this fallback mainly affects truly unparseable strings. The comment says 'it might be a relative URL' which is reasonable, but an explicit check for strings starting with 'javascript:' before the try/catch would be more defense-in-depth.

convertTipTapToInlineHTML applies a second layer of javascript: URI stripping via regex (line 121) after sanitizeRichHTML already blocks them. This is defense-in-depth which is good, but the regex href="javascript:[^"]*" won't catch single-quoted or unquoted href attributes. Since sanitizeRichHTML already handles this correctly and produces double-quoted attributes via escapeAttr, this is not a real vulnerability.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The style attribute sanitization in sanitizeRichHTML only strips CSS expression() but not url(). The comment claims it handles both. This is a documentation-vs-code mismatch that could mislead future workers.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: src/lib/html-utils.ts:170-172 — comment says 'strip any expression() or url() with dangerous protocols' but only expression() regex is applied

sharedStateObservations.observation: TipTap's OrderedList extension is included via StarterKit, and <ol> is in ALLOWED_TAGS, but there's no inline style conversion for <ol> in convertTipTapToInlineHTML() and no <ol> entry in ALLOWED_ATTRS. If a worker later adds ordered list support to the toolbar, the email output won't have proper styling.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: src/lib/html-utils.ts:50 — <ol> not in ALLOWED_ATTRS. src/lib/promotion-email-html.ts — no <ol> handler in convertTipTapToInlineHTML()

sharedStateObservations.observation: escapeAttr() was updated to also escape ampersands (& → &), which is correct for attribute value escaping. This is a positive change that was needed but wasn't explicitly called out in the mission — it's a latent XSS fix for the existing sanitizeTemplateData path.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: src/lib/html-utils.ts:185-188 — escapeAttr now escapes & first, before quotes

summary: Feature newsletter-email-integration passes scrutiny. The implementation correctly integrates newsletter content into email HTML generation with top/bottom positioning, inline style conversion for email compatibility, robust XSS sanitization via sanitizeRichHTML() and isSafeURL(), and fixes for three bugs (javascript: URI vulnerability, TipTap editor external sync, toolbar active state). All 42 tests pass. PreviewColumn correctly passes newsletter data from the store. Import/export round-trip works correctly. Four non-blocking observations documented: (1) CSS url() not stripped in style attributes despite comment saying so, (2) <ol> missing from ALLOWED_ATTRS and convertTipTapToInlineHTML, (3) isSafeURL catch-all could be more defensive, (4) redundant javascript: regex in convertTipTapToInlineHTML only handles double-quoted attributes.
